# OMP Antigravity

> Extension for the Oh My Pi (OMP) coding agent that registers the `antigravity-acp` model provider.
> Each request goes through Google's official Antigravity CLI (`agy acp`) over the Agent Client
> Protocol (ACP), under the user's own Google sign-in. Antigravity serves Gemini, Claude, and GPT-OSS
> models; Oh My Pi keeps its own system prompt, tools, approval policy, and session transcript.
> First release, 0.1.0; tested on macOS arm64. Community project; not affiliated with or endorsed by
> the Oh My Pi maintainers or Google.

## Install

- Requires Oh My Pi, the Antigravity CLI (`agy`), and a Google account signed in to `agy`. Tested on
  macOS arm64 with Oh My Pi `18.18.3` and `18.18.7` and `agy` `1.5.5`. Linux is not live-tested;
  Windows is unsupported.
- Install `agy` with Google's installer (`curl -fsSL https://antigravity.google/cli/install.sh | bash`)
  and sign in once with `agy acp --login`.
- Install the extension pinned to the commit of release 0.1.0:
  `omp plugin install github:alphastorm/omp-antigravity#f0a8720f838e135148211aa7b3aa8a4d4daa1aab`.
- Check the runtime without generating: `/antigravity-doctor` in an Oh My Pi session. Then start a
  session with `omp --model antigravity-acp/gemini-4-argon --thinking high`. In config files and
  agent definitions the selector is `antigravity-acp/<model>:<effort>`.

## Boundaries

- Google's Antigravity terms of service say: "Using third party software, tools, or services to access the Service (e.g. using OpenClaw with Antigravity OAuth) is a breach of this Agreement. Such actions may be grounds for suspension or termination of your Antigravity and/or Gemini CLI accounts."
  Google documents `agy acp` for editors and other ACP clients. Each user reviews the terms and
  judges whether their use is permitted; nothing here is legal advice.
- Google's terms allow human review of interactions and their use for model improvement, subject to
  the account's settings. Everything the model reads (Oh My Pi's system prompt, the user's messages,
  and tool results) goes to Google through `agy`.
- The extension never reads, copies, or refreshes the Google sign-in token; `agy` keeps it in the OS
  keyring. `agy` runs with an allowlisted environment from which API-key and Application Default
  Credentials variables are stripped.
- Each Oh My Pi session runs its own `agy` process in a restricted profile that excludes `agy`'s
  default tools, rules, and skills. Oh My Pi's tools reach the model through a loopback MCP bridge on
  `127.0.0.1` behind a per-session bearer token, and Oh My Pi runs every tool call under its own
  approval policy. A call to any other tool fails the turn.
- `agy` writes each conversation under `~/.omp/antigravity-acp` while a session is open. The
  extension deletes a session's files when its process closes; titles and logs remain until the
  directory is removed.
